title: Dedicated Throughput Metrics Taxonomy (Draft)
body:
Context
- Project: Dedicated throughput SLO + tier definitions
- This doc proposes a first-pass taxonomy for metrics emitted by gateway/runtime/scheduler for Dedicated deployments.
- Primary goals:
  1) Consistent naming + label conventions
  2) Avoid unbounded cardinality (especially deployment_id/model/prompt properties)
  3) Map metrics directly to required dashboard panels + alert rules
  4) Make customer-visible exports feasible without leaking sensitive internal labels

Status / scope
- Draft; subject to revision after we land the metric emission PR (PR-18422) and scheduler instrumentation (PR-18489).
- Applies to Dedicated only (hosted/shared infra metrics are out of scope except where we reuse shared metric names).


1) Measurement principles (high level)
- All SLO/SLI calculations should be computable from Prometheus rate/increase over a fixed window without joining external dimensions.
- Distinguish:
  - "What customers experience" (gateway-level accepted requests, end-to-end tokens) vs
  - "What capacity is doing" (scheduler queue depth, GPU utilization, saturation signals).
- Keep label sets stable across components. Prefer emitting the same metric name from a single layer; if multiple layers must emit similar concepts, encode component in metric name rather than adding a "component" label.


2) Naming conventions
2.1 Metric prefix and separators
- Prefix for all first-party runtime/gateway metrics: redwood_
- Use snake_case. Metric names are nouns with units encoded in suffix.
- Prefer explicit unit suffixes:
  - _seconds, _bytes, _tokens, _requests
  - For rates: keep the base counter in _total, and compute rate() in dashboards/alerts.

2.2 Types
- Counters end with _total
- Gauges do not have a type suffix
- Histograms end with _bucket/_sum/_count (Prometheus conventions)

2.3 Examples
- redwood_dedicated_tokens_output_total (counter)
- redwood_dedicated_request_admitted_total (counter)
- redwood_dedicated_queue_depth_requests (gauge)
- redwood_dedicated_request_latency_seconds_bucket (histogram)


3) Label (dimension) conventions
3.1 Required labels (Dedicated)
These MUST be present on all SLO-relevant metrics unless explicitly called out.
- deployment_id
  - Definition: stable identifier for a Dedicated deployment (customer-specific pool).
  - Cardinality: O(#deployments). Acceptable.
  - NOTE: do not add per-pod/per-replica labels for SLO metrics. Replica-level metrics belong in debug-only families.
- tier
  - Values: standard | performance | premium (final names TBD; keep aligned with Product doc)
  - Cardinality: low.
- region
  - Values: canonical region identifiers (e.g., us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1).
  - Cardinality: low.
- model
  - Values: Redwood model slug pinned at deployment config (e.g., llama-3.1-70b-instruct, qwen2.5-72b-instruct)
  - Cardinality: moderate. Acceptable for Dedicated since deployments are model-pinned; keep model value normalized.

3.2 Optional labels (use sparingly)
- customer_id (INTERNAL ONLY)
  - Avoid in default metrics to reduce blast radius; if needed for internal aggregation, prefer mapping deployment_id -> customer_id in a separate lookup store used by internal tooling.
- endpoint / route
  - Use only at gateway for API endpoint-level breakdowns (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings).
  - Do NOT put full URL/path template; must be enumerated.
- status
  - For request outcomes at gateway: success | error | canceled
  - Avoid raw HTTP status code on high-volume metrics unless explicitly needed; if needed, add http_status_class=2xx|4xx|5xx.
- reason
  - For throttling / shedding: quota | concurrency_limit | burst_limit | overload | maintenance | invalid_request
  - Must be enumerated (no freeform strings).
- phase
  - For tokens/sec instrumentation: prefill | decode

3.3 Labels to avoid (cardinality risks)
- request_id, trace_id, span_id
- prompt_length_bucket derived from raw prompt length (if used, MUST be coarse and enumerated)
- user_id / org_id
- raw model_revision hashes (use stable model slug and a separate model_version label only if needed and enumerated)

3.4 Label ordering (style)
- When documenting metrics and examples, keep labels in this order:
  deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint, status, reason, phase
(Actual ordering is not semantically meaningful in Prometheus, but consistent ordering helps reviews.)


4) Metric families (proposed)
4.1 Throughput (tokens)
A) Output tokens counter (primary for throughput SLO)
- Name: redwood_dedicated_tokens_output_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, phase (optional)
- Semantics: increments by the number of output tokens actually streamed/returned to the client (decode tokens). If phase label is used, phase=decode is the default; phase=prefill can be emitted as separate counter or omitted.
- Used for:
  - Sustained output tokens/sec over window (rate over 5m / 15m depending on SLO spec)
  - By-deployment tier reporting

B) Total tokens counter (optional, internal)
- Name: redwood_dedicated_tokens_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, phase
- Semantics: increments by tokens processed including prefill tokens. NOTE: Can be misleading for customer-experienced throughput; treat as capacity metric.

4.2 Requests (admission, completion, throttling)
A) Requests received
- Name: redwood_dedicated_request_received_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint
- Semantics: request entered gateway, before admission checks.

B) Requests admitted
- Name: redwood_dedicated_request_admitted_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint
- Semantics: request accepted for execution.

C) Requests completed
- Name: redwood_dedicated_request_completed_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint, status
- status values:
  - success: successful completion
  - error: server-side failure after admission
  - canceled: client disconnect / cancel

D) Requests throttled / rejected (expected overload behavior)
- Name: redwood_dedicated_request_throttled_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint, reason
- reason values: quota | concurrency_limit | burst_limit | overload | maintenance | invalid_request
- Guidance:
  - This metric is critical to interpret "low throughput" incidents: sometimes we are correctly enforcing tier limits.

4.3 Latency (end-to-end and serving phase)
A) End-to-end request latency
- Name: redwood_dedicated_request_latency_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint, status
- Semantics: from admission to completion. For streaming, completion is last byte written (or stream close).

B) Time-to-first-token (TTFT)
- Name: redwood_dedicated_ttft_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, endpoint, status
- Semantics: from admission to first streamed token/byte.

C) Decode step latency (scheduler/runtime)
- Name: redwood_dedicated_decode_step_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model
- Semantics: time per decode iteration (internal perf signal; not customer-facing).

4.4 Concurrency and queueing (scheduler)
A) Queue depth
- Name: redwood_dedicated_queue_depth_requests
- Type: gauge
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model
- Semantics: number of admitted requests waiting to be scheduled.

B) In-flight requests
- Name: redwood_dedicated_inflight_requests
- Type: gauge
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model

C) Batch size
- Name: redwood_dedicated_effective_batch_size
- Type: gauge
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model, phase
- phase values: prefill | decode

4.5 Capacity / saturation indicators (infra/runtime)
These should exist but are NOT the Dedicated throughput SLO primary evidence.
A) GPU utilization (if available from exporter)
- Name: redwood_dedicated_gpu_utilization_ratio
- Type: gauge
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model
- Values: 0..1

B) KV cache pressure
- Name: redwood_dedicated_kv_cache_evictions_total
- Type: counter
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model

C) Overload mode state
- Name: redwood_dedicated_overload_mode
- Type: gauge
- Labels: deployment_id, tier, region, model
- Values: 0/1 (or enumerated via separate metric if we need multiple levels)


5) Dashboard panel mapping (Dedicated Throughput SLO dashboards)
This section maps the above metrics to the required panels described in the dashboards spec.

Panel: Throughput (output tokens/sec) by deployment
- Query:
  sum by (deployment_id, tier, region, model) (rate(redwood_dedicated_tokens_output_total[5m]))
- Notes:
  - Compare against tier guarantee line (static per tier + shape; drawn from config)

Panel: Throughput vs throttling (is low throughput due to enforcement?)
- Query:
  rate(redwood_dedicated_request_throttled_total[5m]) / rate(redwood_dedicated_request_received_total[5m])
  broken down by reason

Panel: Admission funnel
- Queries:
  rate(received) vs rate(admitted) vs rate(completed)
  - received: rate(redwood_dedicated_request_received_total[5m])
  - admitted: rate(redwood_dedicated_request_admitted_total[5m])
  - completed: rate(redwood_dedicated_request_completed_total[5m])

Panel: Queue depth + inflight
- Queries:
  redwood_dedicated_queue_depth_requests
  redwood_dedicated_inflight_requests
- Notes:
  - High queue depth with low inflight may indicate scheduler bottleneck or stuck workers.

Panel: Tail latency guardrails (p95)
- Queries:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, deployment_id, endpoint) (rate(redwood_dedicated_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, deployment_id, endpoint) (rate(redwood_dedicated_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])))

Panel: Saturation / utilization
- Queries:
  avg by (deployment_id) (redwood_dedicated_gpu_utilization_ratio)
  rate(redwood_dedicated_kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])
  redwood_dedicated_overload_mode

Panel: Model + region breakdown (rollup view)
- Query:
  sum by (tier, region, model) (rate(redwood_dedicated_tokens_output_total[15m]))


6) Customer-visible vs internal metrics
Customer-visible export candidates (safe + interpretable)
- redwood_dedicated_tokens_output_total (aggregated)
- redwood_dedicated_request_admitted_total
- redwood_dedicated_request_completed_total
- redwood_dedicated_request_throttled_total (reason aggregated, no internal-only reasons)
- redwood_dedicated_request_latency_seconds (histogram)
- redwood_dedicated_ttft_seconds (histogram)
- redwood_dedicated_queue_depth_requests (optional; may confuse, but useful for advanced customers)

Internal-only (debug / capacity)
- GPU utilization, KV cache pressure, decode step latency, effective batch size

Rule of thumb
- If a metric can be misinterpreted as "Redwood is slow" when it is actually "customer is sending pathological prompts" then keep it internal unless paired with clear guidance.


7) Implementation notes / instrumentation ownership
Gateway (API edge)
- Owns: request_received/admitted/completed, latency, TTFT, throttled (with reason)
- Key requirement: ensure admitted/completed counters align with SLI definition (exclusions for maintenance, invalid requests, etc. should be encoded via reason/status + SLI filters).

Runtime/Scheduler
- Owns: tokens_output_total (source of truth), queue depth, inflight, batch size, decode instrumentation
- Risk: token counting discrepancies for streaming + retries. Decision: count tokens only once per successful emission to client; for mid-stream disconnect, tokens already emitted should still be counted in output_total (customer received them).

Infra exporters
- Owns: GPU utilization, memory, NIC. Must map to deployment_id without adding per-GPU UUID labels.


8) Cardinality budget (practical guidance)
- Every timeseries is a combination of metric name + labelset.
- Dedicated cardinality drivers are (deployment_id x model x endpoint x status x reason).
- Hard guidance for reviewers:
  - endpoint: max 5 values
  - status: max 3 values
  - reason: max ~8 values
  - Do not add both endpoint and model to high-frequency per-token metrics unless necessary. For tokens_output_total, endpoint is not needed.


9) Open questions (need decisions)
1) Do we include model_version label for pinned deployments?
   - Pros: clearer rollouts
   - Cons: doubles cardinality; may be redundant if model slug includes version
   - Proposal: do NOT add model_version in v1. Encode in model slug or attach as annotation in config/dashboards.

2) TTFT definition for non-streaming requests
   - Option A: TTFT = latency (first token equals last)
   - Option B: TTFT not recorded
   - Proposal: A, for consistent histograms.

3) How do we label prefill vs decode tokens?
   - Proposal: Keep primary counter output-only. Add separate internal counter for total tokens with phase label if needed.

4) deployment_id naming / lifecycle
   - Need confirmation from control plane: deployment_id stability across resizes and shape changes. If it changes, we need a stable deployment_uid.

5) Maintenance carve-outs
   - How to reflect planned maintenance in metrics so SLO toolkit can exclude windows?
   - Proposal: emit throttled_total{reason="maintenance"} and/or a dedicated gauge redwood_dedicated_maintenance_mode, and have SLO tooling exclude time ranges from SLI calculation based on maintenance_mode.


10) Next steps
- Logan: update ENG-2194 checklist to match names/labels above.
- Sergio: validate dashboard queries in observability-pack/pr-611 against this taxonomy; call out any missing dimensions.
- Aisha/Rafael: confirm SLO tooling filters (which status/reason values count toward SLI vs exclusions).
- Omar/Noah: confirm token counting source-of-truth and streaming edge cases.

Changelog
- 2025-01-29: Initial draft created (Logan)
- 2025-02-05: Added throttling reason enums + customer-visible section (Logan + Sergio)
- 2025-02-12: Added cardinality budget guidance + dashboard panel mapping updates (Logan + Aisha)
